questions.question: Name two personal hygiene practices required for meat handlers.
questions.solution_html:
• Wash hands thoroughly before handling meat.
  • Wear clean protective clothing and keep fingernails short.
questions.final_answer: Wash hands thoroughly before handling meat

questions.question: Define modified atmosphere packaging (MAP) and mention any two gases / used in MAP.
questions.solution_html:
• MAP.
  • MAP is a packaging technique in which the natural atmosphere inside a package is replaced with
  • a controlled gas mixture to extend the shelf life of food.
  • Two gases used are carbon dioxide (CO₂) and nitrogen (N₂).
questions.final_answer: Two gases used are carbon dioxide (CO₂) and nitrogen (N₂)

questions.question: Illustrate the distribution of proteins in different parts of poultry meat.
questions.solution_html:
• Breast meat contains a higher proportion of white muscle fibres, while leg meat contains
  • more red muscle fibres and myoglobin. Both breast and leg muscles contain myofibrillar
  • proteins (actin and myosin), sarcoplasmic proteins and connective tissue proteins.
questions.final_answer: proteins (actin and myosin), sarcoplasmic proteins and connective tissue proteins

questions.question: Define rigor mortis.
questions.solution_html:
• Rigor mortis is the stiffening of muscles after slaughter due to ATP depletion and the
  • formation of stable actin–myosin cross-bridges.
  • It occurs during post-mortem changes in meat and affects meat tenderness
questions.final_answer: It occurs during post-mortem changes in meat and affects meat tenderness

questions.question: List two advantages of meat irradiation.
questions.solution_html:
• List two advantages of meat irradiation.
  • Reduces pathogenic microorganisms and improves food safety.
  • Delays spoilage and extends the shelf life of meat.
questions.final_answer: Delays spoilage and extends the shelf life of meat

questions.question: Differentiate between fresh water fish and marine fish?
questions.solution_html:
• Freshwater fish: Live in rivers, lakes and ponds; examples include rohu and catla.
  • Marine fish: Live in seas and oceans; examples include sardine and mackerel.

questions.question: Write a note on mechanical tenderization of meat.
questions.solution_html:
• Mechanical tenderization involves breaking muscle fibres and connective tissues using blades
  • needles, pounding or cubing equipment.
  • It improves meat tenderness and eating quality; however, blade or needle tenderization may
  • transfer surface microorganisms into the interior of the meat
questions.final_answer: transfer surface microorganisms into the interior of the meat
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Discuss the advantages of hot smoking in meat preservation.
questions.solution_html:
• Hot smoking combines heat treatment, drying and smoke deposition to reduce microbial load
  • and improve flavour, colour and texture.
  • It helps extend shelf life by reducing moisture and microbial growth, although proper cooking
  • cooling and storage are essential for safety.
questions.final_answer: cooling and storage are essential for safety
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Describe the preparation of fish silage and its uses?
questions.solution_html:
• Fish silage is prepared by mincing fish waste or whole fish, adding an acid such as formic acid
  • and allowing enzymes to break down the fish tissues into a liquid product.
  • It is used as an ingredient in animal and aquaculture feeds and as a source of proteins, peptides
  • and nutrients.
questions.final_answer: and nutrients
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Describe the major factors considered in grading meat.
questions.solution_html:
• Carcass characteristics: Age, sex, carcass weight, conformation, muscle development and fat
  • distribution.
  • Meat quality: Colour, texture, marbling, tenderness and maturity.
questions.final_answer: Meat quality: Colour, texture, marbling, tenderness and maturity
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Describe the physical changes occurring in meat during cooking.
questions.solution_html:
• Muscle proteins denature and coagulate, causing changes in colour, firmness and texture;
  • muscle fibres shrink as the temperature increases.
  • Fat melts, moisture is lost, collagen gradually converts to gelatin during prolonged moist
  • cooking, and the meat decreases in weight and volume.
questions.final_answer: cooking, and the meat decreases in weight and volume
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Implement suitable handling, packaging and storage practices to maintain the / quality and safety of eggs during storage.
questions.solution_html:
• Implement suitable handling, packaging and storage practices to maintain the quality
  • and safety of eggs during storage.
  • Handling and packaging: Handle eggs gently, reject cracked or dirty eggs, maintain clean
  • conditions, and use clean, protective cartons to prevent breakage and contamination.
  • Storage: Store eggs under refrigeration at a consistent temperature, preferably around 4°C or
  • below, maintain the cold chain, and follow the recommended shelf life and stock rotation
  • practices.
  • Long Essay Questions
questions.final_answer: Long Essay Questions
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain the structural and sanitary features required for hygienic slaughter and / meat processing in a modern abattoir.
questions.solution_html:
• processing in a modern abattoir.
  • Structural features: The abattoir should have separate areas for animal reception, lairage
  • slaughter, dressing, carcass inspection and meat processing, with impervious floors, adequate
  • drainage, ventilation, lighting and a reliable water supply.
  • Sanitary features: Proper cleaning and disinfection, hygienic equipment, personal protective
  • clothing, pest control, safe waste disposal, potable water and separation of clean and
  • contaminated areas are essential to prevent cross-contamination.
questions.final_answer: contaminated areas are essential to prevent cross-contamination
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain the complete procedure of post-mortem inspection of carcasses and / edible organs.
questions.solution_html:
• organs. U]
  • Carcass examination: Inspect the carcass visually for abnormalities, bruises, lesions, swelling
  • and contamination; examine and palpate relevant lymph nodes and make incisions where
  • required to detect disease.
  • Organ examination and disposition: Examine the liver, lungs, heart, kidneys, spleen and other
  • edible organs for lesions, parasites and abnormalities; correlate findings with ante-mortem
  • observations and pass, partially condemn or condemn the carcass and affected organs as
  • appropriate.
questions.final_answer: appropriate
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain the importance of pH changes after slaughter in relation to PSE and / DFD meat.
questions.solution_html:
• meat.
  • PSE meat (Pale, Soft and Exudative): Rapid post-mortem glycolysis while the carcass is still
  • warm causes a rapid pH decline, resulting in pale colour, soft texture and excessive drip loss.
  • DFD meat (Dark, Firm and Dry): Depletion of muscle glycogen before slaughter results in
  • insufficient lactic acid production and a high ultimate pH, producing dark, firm meat with a
  • sticky surface and reduced shelf life due to increased microbial growth.
questions.final_answer: sticky surface and reduced shelf life due to increased microbial growth
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain the production, properties, advantages and agricultural application of / fish manure?
questions.solution_html:
• manure?
  • Production and properties: Fish manure is produced from fish waste by decomposition
  • fermentation or composting, sometimes with other organic materials; it contains nitrogen
  • phosphorus, potassium and other nutrients, along with organic matter.
  • Advantages and agricultural applications: It improves soil fertility, supplies nutrients to crops
  • supports beneficial soil microorganisms and promotes plant growth; it can be applied as compost
  • or processed organic fertilizer after suitable treatment to ensure hygienic safety.
questions.final_answer: or processed organic fertilizer after suitable treatment to ensure hygienic safety
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
